problem: Existing embodied task-planning benchmarks rely on manual curation, have short/simple tasks, and rarely test spatial (relation, occlusion) and temporal/causal understanding; EQA benchmarks lack interaction with an environment for re-planning.
motivation: LLM/VLM-based high-level planners are known to be weak at spatial and temporal reasoning, yet there is no scalable, automatically generated, fine-grained diagnostic benchmark for it. A controllable task generator with simulator feedback lets difficulty be scaled by adding constraints, and provides data to fine-tune small models.
key_idea: An LLM-assisted, simulator-verified pipeline that generates unlimited embodied navigation/manipulation tasks with controllable spatial (relation, occlusion, layout map) and temporal/causal (multi-object, dependency, two-arm optimal path) constraints, evaluated with an LLM-agent baseline in VirtualHome and Habitat.
insight: Success drops sharply when spatial relation constraints are added (Navi 79.26% -> 62.61% for GPT-4; Navi&Mani 73.76% -> 49.65%), and a prior layout map raises it (90.77%), showing spatial verification and exploration are the bottlenecks. Small Llama-7B SFT'd on ~5.5K benchmark-generated QA pairs matches GPT-4, showing the generated data is useful for training. CoT and few-shot prompting give negligible gains.
method: Task template generation: per-task-type template with description placeholders and completion criteria as relation predicates (e.g. (CLOSE, robot, fridge) & (INSIDE, apple, fridge)).
Scene-graph info gathering: query simulator scene graph to shortlist object combinations satisfying template constraints (e.g. INSIDE).

LLM-assisted task generation and filtering: LLM composes and rephrases commonsense tasks with rules/examples, then tasks not executable in the simulator are discarded; human check found 4-8% unreasonable tasks.

Ground-truth plan generation: shortest path from scene graph translated into executable action sequences (walk/grab/put); temporal tasks decomposed into sub-tasks; two-arm vs one-arm plans compared for optimal path.

Task categories/difficulty axes: navigation, navigation+manipulation, relation constraint, occlusion by small size (smallest 20%) or distance (farthest 20%), layout-map prior, multi-object, temporal dependency.

LLM agent baseline: task classification, LLM ranks rooms, 360° scan, LLM picks large visible objects to explore, memory of seen objects, manipulation skills, completion check with max step budget; perception via VirtualHome API (Grounding-DINO in Habitat).
Metrics: success rate, sequence length, LCS length and ratio vs GT, moving distance.

setting.backbone: GPT-4 (frozen) as main agent; Llama3-70B, Mistral-8x7B, Llama3-8B (frozen); LLAMA2-7B (SFT)
setting.training_data: SFT of LLAMA2-7B on 5457 GPT-4-generated QA pairs from 34 VirtualHome layouts (nav, nav+relation, nav&mani, nav&mani+relation); others zero-shot
setting.observation: VirtualHome API visible-object graph (text object lists) from 360° scans; Grounding-DINO detections in Habitat
setting.action_space: High-level skills: WALK to object/room, TURNRIGHT 30°, OPEN, CLOSE, GRAB, PUT, PUTIN
setting.privileged: VirtualHome perception API provides visible objects; layout-map variant gives locations of large furniture; full scene graph variant used for GT only

numbers.bench: other:ET-Plan-Bench (Navi & Mani + Multi Objects + Temp Dependency)

numbers_note: Benchmark is the paper's own (no canonical benchmark); split labelled 'test' as held-out layouts. Only a subset of table rows listed.
results: GPT-4 agent reaches 79.26% on plain navigation but drops to 62.61% with relation constraints and 49.65% for nav&mani with relations; temporal-dependency tasks reach 58.60%. Llama3-70B and Mixtral-8x7B match GPT-4, Llama3-8B collapses to 27.74% on Navi+Relation, and SFT Llama-7B matches or slightly beats GPT-4 (80.58% vs 79.26% Navi).
limitations: Only two simulators, sim-to-real gap; perception relies on the VirtualHome API since VLM detectors are slow and low accuracy
Spatial reasoning excludes left/right; LLM-generated tasks still have 4-8% unreasonable cases
Baseline agent is a hand-designed pipeline; results depend on it, and benchmark code was not yet released
